transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-02
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alyssa Park (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Sundial Head of ML), Markus Lee (Infra), Talia Gomez (Product), Samir Patel (joined late)

Auto-summary: Walkthrough of Redwood Optimize console focusing on prefetch (KV), batching, and cost sims. Discussed Sundial SLA (2.5s p95), constraints around on-prem VPC and KMS. Actions: sandboxes, cost spreadsheet, perf sim.

---Transcript body---
[00:00] Alyssa: hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Alyssa from Redwood, i'll hand off to diego for the deep console walk — but first quick round robin.
[00:12] Priya: hi, priya here — head of ml at sundial, we run a conversational assistant for field techs. SLA targets are tight, about 2.5s p95 with occasional long contexts up to 1k tokens.
[00:25] Markus: markus, infra, we care about predictable cost and also need VPC & KMS since some PII flows through the model.
[00:32] Talia: product, we want to understand uplift vs risk and how rollouts would look.
[00:38] Diego: great, i'll jump into the console. quick note: i've uploaded a toy trace similar to your traffic (not your data) to run the sim. i'll show two scenarios: naive serving, and lookahead KV prefetch + adaptive batching.
[01:05] Diego: opening Console -> Optimize -> Simulations. you'll see the baseline row — model m-open-ggml-lite (note: model names may be slightly different in my env). baseline p50/p95 tokens cost etc.
[01:28] Priya: quick q — when you say lookahead, is that the same as prefix cache? we sometimes call it session caching or KV.
[01:35] Diego: yes similar. technically we maintain a KV cache keyed by session + prefix id and we can prefetch expected KV entries for typical prompts — reduces repeated forward passes. some customers call it prefix cache, others call it lookahead prefetch.
[01:48] Markus: does prefetch increase memory? we have limited GPU RAM on dedicated nodes.
[01:52] Diego: good question — prefetch trades memory for throughput. the console shows estimated KV memory delta per shard. in our sim i set conservative prefetch depth of 3 entries, bumping KV memory usage ~12%. but tokens served per GPU/second increased 1.8x in the sim.
[02:18] Talia: can you show the cost model? how are you calc'ing the savings.
[02:23] Diego: sure — open Cost Model tab. we combine per-token execution cost, reserved capacity amortization, and prefix hit rate. you'll see an input called 'sessionization window' — that's how we cluster requests per session to enable prefix hits.
[02:38] [Diego shares screen: shows a spreadsheet style cost model with toggles: batch size, concurrency, prefetch depth, KV hit rate, reserved vs hosted pricing]
[03:05] Priya: our median sequence length is around 120 tokens but we have long tail up to 1k, how do you account for that?
[03:12] Diego: the sim accepts a distribution or real trace. i loaded your anonymized trace (toy) and the sim computed sequence length buckets. cost numbers in the console are weighted by frequency. that's why the long-tail matters a lot for caching benefits — repeated prefixes on long sessions give big wins.
[03:35] Markus: i want to call out security — when prefetching do you persist KV on disk? encryption?
[03:41] Alyssa: short answer: KV can be kept in-memory on the serving tier; for Private customers with on-prem we support encrypted persistence with KMS integration. audit logs show KV hits/evictions. we'll share the security whitepaper and KMS integration doc.
[03:59] Priya: ok pls share the whitepaper.
[04:02] Diego: moving on — batching. the console sim lets you set max batch size and target latency SLO. see here: i toggled 'latency budget 2.5s p95' and increased batching aggressiveness for background requests but kept interactive path lower.
[04:25] Diego: (note: sometimes transcription says batch size 8 but in practice we use continuous batching so effective size varies with concurrency).
[04:37] [04:37] Talia: how do fallbacks work if prefetch hits are low and a model variant is cheaper but slower?
[04:44] Diego: we have routing policies — cost-first, latency-first, region-priority. you can set automatic fallback to quantized variants when latency allows, or prefer higher-capacity dedicated pools. the console preview shows expected regrets if fallback triggers.
[05:07] Priya: can we see a scenario where prefetch hurts latency? i.e., prefetch adds overhead when hit rate is low.
[05:14] Diego: yes — i created scenario 'sparse-prefixes' in sim. in that case prefetch adds serialization overhead and memory churn; the console flags net-negative cases. we recommend enabling prefetch only when expected hit rate > ~15% for your workload.
[05:36] Markus: curious about sessionization: what's the window you used? 10 minutes? 30?
[05:41] Diego: for this sim i used 20 minutes default. the console shows sensitivity sweeps: 5/20/60 minutes — longer windows increase hit rate but also KV memory footprint and staleness.
[05:57] [06:05] Samir (joined): sorry late, can you recap the difference between prefix/prefetch and KV session cache?
[06:12] Diego: quick recap — session KV stores tokens/keys for a session for reuse; prefix prefetch proactively loads likely next KV entries before model step; both reduce recomputation but with different tradeoffs.
[06:28] Priya: is the prefetch logic client-side or server-side?
[06:32] Diego: server-side inside Redwood runtime. we expose hooks to provide signals (e.g., intent) but the decision lives in the serving layer.
[06:40] Talia: what about routing across regions? we need EU-only traffic for some customers.
[06:45] Alyssa: you can pin models and prefetch configs per region; console allows per-region SLOs and cost breakdowns. we'll show the multi-region tab in the follow-up sandbox.
[06:58] Diego: switching to a micro-sim: baseline vs prefetch+batching. baseline: p95 latency 2.7s, cost $0.22 per 1k tokens. optimized: p95 2.3s, cost $0.14 per 1k tokens — numbers here use reserved capacity assumptions.
[07:27] Priya: that ~36% cost reduction looks promising. how brittle are these numbers to model changes? say we swap to a 7B quantized variant.
[07:34] Diego: the console 'what-if' lets you change model family. for a quantized 7B, token exec cost drops, but prefetch benefit usually shrinks because compute is cheaper relative to KV overhead. still often net positive if you have repeat prefixes.
[07:56] Markus: storage and eviction policy for KV? LRU? TTL?
[08:00] Diego: default LRU + per-session TTL. console exposes TTL per policy. you can also pin certain prefixes to longer retention.
[08:10] [08:15] Talia: are there built-in metrics I can pull into our observability? we use Grafana/Datadog.
[08:20] Alyssa: yes — we export token-level, KV hit/miss, batching size histograms, and cost counters. there are tracing hooks to correlate request id to model version and KV hits.
[08:32] Priya: can we get a sample dashboard?
[08:35] Alyssa: will share Grafana dashboard JSON with the sandbox.
[08:38] Diego: showing the 'risk' panel: console flags cases where prefetch increases p95 or when KV growth crosses threshold. it's not just a number — there are alarms you can attach to rollout policies.
[08:53] Markus: on the private deployment side, does prefetch work if we run on-prem with strict egress?
[08:59] Diego: yes — prefetch logic runs in the private serving plane. egress only for optional telemetry if you enable it; otherwise telemetry can be on-prem too. KMS calls can be proxied to your HSM.
[09:15] Priya: what was the overhead latency of lookahead prefetch itself? does it add an extra hop?
[09:20] Diego: prefetch is async in the pipeline; it can add microseconds on miss, but when it hits it removes entire forward passes. net latency lowers for hit rates above threshold. the console shows per-request latency component breakdown.
[09:37] [10:02] Diego: demo: toggling prefetch depth showing hit rates from 8% -> 34%, cost curves update. note the knee in the graph where memory costs start to dominate.
[10:22] Priya: our ops team is nervous about automatic eviction complexity — can we start with a conservative manual policy?
[10:28] Alyssa: absolutely. many customers pilot with manual TTL and a conservative prefetch depth, then enable adaptive tuning after observing telemetry for a week.
[10:36] Talia: about rollouts — can we canary prefetch settings?
[10:39] Diego: yes canary by user slice, session attribute, or region. console wizards help create canary policies and observe delta metrics.
[10:50] [11:10] Diego: now the concurrency dimension. the sim shows at low concurrency (<8 concurrent sessions) batching doesn't help much; at high concurrency (>40) batching amortizes kernel overhead dramatically.
[11:24] Markus: our peak concurrent sessions are roughly 120 across 4 nodes. what cluster size did you assume?
[11:30] Diego: sim assumed 6 GPUs with continuous batching. we can swap to your cluster config in the sandbox.
[11:37] Samir: will the simulator accept our real trace? we want to include bot-rest and human-in-the-loop flows.
[11:42] Diego: yes — you can upload gzipped traces. we'll sign an NDA for any real traces you share. for the demo i used a synthetic trace that matches your histogram.
[11:55] Priya: how are warm-started KV states handled across restarts?
[12:00] Diego: we persist checkpoints optionally so session KV can be restored; for ephemeral sessions we only keep in memory. persistence is configurable and encrypted.
[12:12] [12:30] Diego: sharing links in chat: console-sandbox.s.redwood.io/ss-sandbox (demo), optimize-playbook-v2.xlsx (cost model), security-whitepaper.pdf
[12:45] Talia: got them.
[12:48] Diego: quick Q&A: any blockers for running the perf sim?
[12:54] Priya: only security signoff; need SSO/SAML contact.
[12:58] Markus: and we need an on-prem checklist for HSM/KMS.
[13:04] Alyssa: noted — i'll include both in the follow-up email.
[13:07] Priya: how do you price Dedicated vs Hosted for pilots? we prefer a month-long pilot.
[13:13] Alyssa: pilots are typically a short Dedicated reservation or a hosted sandbox with usage caps. i'll attach a price comparison in the sheet.
[13:22] Diego: demo: 'what-if' for quantized 7b + prefetch: cost down, prefetch benefit shrinks but latency still improved in our trace.
[13:44] Talia: curious if this approach interacts poorly with tool-calling / function calls in chat.
[13:49] Diego: tool-calls can be treated as branching prefixes — we fold them into session keys. the console flags tool-heavy flows where prefetch is less effective and suggests different batching profiles.
[14:10] Priya: any known reliability concerns at scale? e.g., cache thrashing during flash crowds.
[14:16] Diego: yes flash crowds can thrash KV; we recommend adaptive TTLs and dynamic shard rebalancing, which console can simulate. also automatic fallback to non-prefetch routing during thrash.
[14:31] Markus: do you support metrics export granularity per-token? that could be noisy.
[14:35] Alyssa: yes it's optional and sampled; defaults are aggregated to per-minute histograms.
[14:45] [15:00] Diego: running a mid-sim sensitivity sweep: varying concurrency 10->150 and plotting cost per request. you'll see a crossover where batching gains explode past 60 concurrency.
[15:28] Priya: how do you recommend we start the pilot? small user slice? all users in a region?
[15:34] Diego: common pattern: start with 5-10% user slice in lower-risk region, conservative prefetch depth 1-2, manual TTL, observe 48-72 hours, then ramp. console wizards can auto-run ramp.
[15:49] Talia: what about QA — can we replay traffic?
[15:52] Diego: yes sandbox supports traffic replays from the trace. we can also run canary replays against your staging endpoint.
[15:59] [16:15] Alyssa: ok wrapping up, recap and owners — alyssa sends cost sheet + security docs; diego runs perf sim with your trace; priya provides SSO contact.
[16:26] Priya: sounds good. thanks.
[16:29] Markus: thanks all.
[16:31] Talia: cheers.
[16:32] Diego: thanks, we'll follow up with the sandbox invite.
[16:36] [call ends]

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hearings present (model names slightly different, speaker tags for late joiner), filler words and overlaps preserved.

References shared in chat: https://console-sandbox.s.redwood.io/ss-sandbox, https://files.redwood/optimize-playbook-v2.xlsx, https://files.redwood/security-whitepaper.pdf
